K3c.prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic close-up still, 16:9, soft natural daylight, shallow depth of field. The same bright treatment room, the same patient and the same cosmetologist as in the first reference image, a moment later in the same facial treatment, now framed as a close-up.

The patient (exactly the woman from the first reference image: late twenties, fair skin with light redness and a few faint post-acne marks on her cheek, no inflamed spots, light-blond hair tucked under the same white disposable cap, the same plain white T-shirt) lies on her back on the white treatment couch with her eyes closed, calm. Her head fills the left half of the frame, seen in profile from her left side: her face looks up, the chin toward the lower left, the white cap toward the centre of the frame, her left cheek and ear turned to the camera. Her skin is clean and dry, natural skin texture.

The cosmetologist's right hand in the same white disposable glove comes in from the upper right corner of the frame and holds a syringe just above the patient's cheek, the way a professional doses a product: the index and middle fingers under the round finger flange, the thumb resting on the round plate of the plunger. The syringe lies diagonally across the centre of the frame, its tip at the lower left, a few millimetres above the skin of the cheek below the cheekbone, its plunger at the upper right. She is laying the serum on the working zones of the face drop by drop: four small glossy, almost colourless translucent drops already sit on the cheek and cheekbone, about two centimetres apart, and one more small drop is forming at the tip of the syringe. Nothing is injected: there is no needle, and the tip does not touch the skin.

The syringe is exactly the real syringe from the second reference image (three photographs of the same syringe and an upright view of its label) - copy it, do not redesign it: a slim, long, clear plastic syringe; a large clear round finger flange; a clear plunger rod with a clear round thumb plate; a white matte paper label wrapped around almost the whole length of the barrel. The label side with the brand name faces the camera: the word MITODERM in large, thin, widely spaced black capital letters running along the barrel, starting near the tip, and directly under it, in smaller black capitals, BIOSPICULE PROFESSIONAL. The small clear cap has been taken off the tip: the syringe ends in its short clear collar with a small clear nozzle. No needle, no coloured or black rubber stopper, no scale marks, no other print, not thicker, not shorter. About half of the plunger rod is visible between the flange and the thumb plate.

Of the cosmetologist only the gloved right hand, the wrist and a part of the forearm in the white uniform sleeve are in the frame, slightly soft; her face is not in the frame. Behind them the room is softly blurred: warm pale-beige wall, bright window light on the right. Keep the patient's face, the hand and the whole syringe inside the left 60% of the frame.

The only text in the image is the print on the syringe label. No captions, no logos elsewhere, no watermark, no arrows, no drawn marks.
